name: Hippogryph Harassment

angles.text: As a night elf, you revere hippogryphs as sacred companions of Elune. Culling an aggressive wild flock is a somber task when wilderness clashes with traveler safety.
As a hunter, you understand the predatory instincts of aerial beasts and the hierarchy of a wild roost. Killing the matriarch is the surest way to break the flock's aggression.
As a druid, you seek harmony with the wild. You can see this culling as an unfortunate necessity to restore balance after the beasts began preying on travelers.

faq.answer: The hippogryphs have established nesting grounds southeast of Shen'dar Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. Their territory lies beside the main travel route, and they attack those who come near to defend their brood and hunting grounds.
faq.q: Why are the hippogryphs attacking travelers near Shen'dar Village?

faq.answer: The flock nests southeast of Shen'dar Village in the Shen'dar Highlands. Its roost overlooks the road, where the young, protectors, and matriarch gather among the cliffs and ridges.
faq.q: Where is the hippogryph flock located?

faq.answer: To restore safe travel, slay eight hippogryph youths, six sturdy hippogryph protectors, and the hippogryph matriarch who directs the roost in the Shen'dar Highlands.
faq.q: Which hippogryphs must be slain to complete the task?

faq.answer: A powerful Hippogryph Matriarch leads the flock in the Shen'dar Highlands. She directs the roost and its defense of the nesting grounds southeast of Shen'dar Village, so her death is needed to break the flock's hold on the roadway.
faq.q: Who is the leader of the hippogryph flock?

faq.answer: The youths are the flock's future growth and continued expansion. Culling them alongside the mature protectors keeps the roost from quickly replenishing its strength or establishing a lasting reign of terror over the local highways.
faq.q: Why must the hippogryph youths be culled?

faq.answer: No. These are wild, untamed creatures that established a roost in the Shen'dar Highlands on their own. Unlike the disciplined mounts raised by the night elves, this feral flock treats any passing humanoid as an intruder or prey encroaching on its territory.
faq.q: Are these hippogryphs tame or allied with anyone?

faq.answer: The flock nests overlooking the road leading southeast from Shen'dar Village. The beasts swoop down on supply carts, messengers, and wandering travelers, threatening safe overland travel and risking the village's isolation from the surrounding lands.
faq.q: What danger do these hippogryphs pose to the local settlement?

sections.body:
Travelers near Shen'dar Village face danger from the skies. A wild flock nests southeast of the settlement, in the Shen'dar Highlands. Across Kalimdor, hippogryphs are known as noble beasts, and some are bonded to elven riders. Untamed flocks, though, fiercely guard their territory.

Wagons and lone travelers on the paths below have become targets of aerial ambushes. The attacks disrupt passage and could leave the village isolated if the creatures go unchecked.
sections.title: Peril on the Road

sections.body:
The flock's nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands must be confronted to end the danger. To make the high roads safe, kill the young before they reach maturity and overcome the vigilant protectors guarding the perimeter.

The matriarch directs attacks on passersby. Travelers can use the roads safely again only when the nest is struck and she is felled.
sections.title: Culling the Flock

summary: Near Shen'dar Village, Hippogryph Harassment puts travelers in danger. A wild flock nests southeast of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands and attacks those on the nearby road. You are asked to cull its young, protectors, and matriarch so travelers can pass safely.
